# Issue 113 diagnostic matrix

The deterministic corpus is retained from the measured source
`b573bf6efadf0bdad83cb26188206e9daabd2771`. Regeneration changes no contracts,
iterations, predicates or arm representations. The depth-1000 B source has
1000 aliases, and its manifest size is 1000; older copied 100-alias B results
cannot be its denominator. Generic-nesting fixtures price the declared nested
instantiation path and concrete witness; they are not a universal arbitrary-depth
compiled-value benchmark.

All thirteen extended families and separate depth, generic-nesting,
function-identity, function-creation and generic-boundary jobs run with
Z3 5.1.0 and 4.12.1, seed 0. RU comparisons use one solver/version/seed.
Existing source/proof flags, 16M resource limit, 60s VC cap, 90s process cap,
32-case/120-command ceilings, samples and max-parallel 12 remain unchanged.
Runtime/build/allocation stages run only on the 5.1.0 axis after matching
positive warning-free prerequisite reports. Missing, rejected, timed-out,
warning-bearing and skipped arms remain explicit recorded outcomes; successful
Actions dispatch is not semantic acceptance.

The original arbitrary cross-signature arrow coercion controls remain under
`limits/arrow-coercion`; their unproved contracts are separate from this corpus's
shared exact-base/runtime contracts and must not be reported as repaired.

Compiler identity binds every actual published DLL and JSON configuration plus
the native apphost. Matching source, manifest and solver bytes are also required
between proof/build/run reports. The archive receipt records its own hash and
last product revision. Apphost identity alone is insufficient.

Resolution memory uses existing GNU time peak RSS for the whole resolve command,
including startup/parsing; it is not a separate internal resolver phase metric.
Quantifier-instantiation counters are recorded only if already present in CSV or
stdout/stderr. No extra prover/statistics flag or seed is introduced. Missing
counters remain unavailable; syntactic Boogie quantifier counts are not solver
instantiations.

C# allocation profiles keep the original Work body inside the reviewed try/finally
instrumentation. No warning filter, NoWarn expansion, nullable change or build
optimization change is made. The existing codatatype lazy-cache CS8618 is a native
compiler warning also present in the original emitted source. The ordinary Dafny
C# backend hides successful dotnet output; its quiet log does not prove that
warning absent. If the exact final product still emits it, allocation profiles
remain unavailable under the existing warning gate. Ordinary runtime success
cannot supply missing allocation evidence.

These are public diagnostic GitHub measurements; the alternate solver axis is
not a trusted queued project gate. The final product and actual compiler receipt
must be reviewed independently of older focused b573 measurements.
